Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:10:1.hebrew: זרק - מזיק כלים מראש הגג, והיו תחתיו כרים וכסתות כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:10:1.english: Threw - [If] a damager [threw] vessels from the top of the roof, and there were cushions and blankets beneath it, etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:10:2.hebrew: פטור - שהרי מזריקתו אין סופו לישבר עד שינטלו הכרים. וזה שנטל הכרים — ואפילו הזורק עצמו נטלן — פטור, דגרמא בניזקין הוי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:10:2.english: Exempt - For as a result of his throw, it would not ultimately break unless the cushions were removed. And the one who removed the cushions — even if the thrower himself removed them — is exempt, because it is indirect causation (gerama) in damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:1:1.english: From where [are] these matters [derived] - That [regarding] damage, [one is] liable even [when] unintentional.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:1:2.hebrew: פצע תחת פצע - קרא יתירא הוא להך דרשה, דהא כתיב "כי יתן מום בעמיתו כאשר עשה וגו'", וכויה וחבורה דרשינן בהחובל (לקמן בבא קמא דף פד:):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:1:2.english: Wound for wound - It is a superfluous verse [written] for this exposition, for it is [already] written: "If a man inflicts a blemish upon his fellow, as he has done, etc." [Leviticus 24:19]; and [as for] "burn" and "bruise" [mentioned there], we expound [them] in [the chapter] HaChovel (below, Bava Kamma 84b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:2:1.hebrew: במקום נזק - דאפי' היכא דאיכא נזק משלם נמי צער, דלא תימא צער דכתבה רחמנא היינו בדליכא נזק, כגון כוואו בשפוד על צפרנו דלא אפחתיה מכספיה. ולהך דרשה מפקינן ליה בהחובל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:2:1.english: In a case of damage - That even where there is damage, he also pays [for] pain, so that you should not say [that the] pain that the Merciful One wrote [in the Torah] is [only] where there is no damage — such as where he burned him with a spit on his fingernail, where he did not diminish his [monetary] value — and for that exposition we derive it in [the chapter] HaChovel.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:3:1.english: With regard to damages, [he is] liable - For we derived [that] an unwitting [actor is treated] like an intentional [one], and one [acting] under duress like one [acting] willingly.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:3:2.hebrew: מלאכת מחשבת אסרה תורה - שנתכוין לעשות מלאכה, אלא כסבור שהיום חול או סבור שמלאכה זו מותרת. וכל הני דאמרינן הכא, לא נתכוונו לעשות המלאכה, הלכך פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:3:2.english: The Torah prohibited planned labor - [Meaning a case where] he intended to perform a labor, but [he] thought that today is a weekday or thought that this labor is permitted. And [in] all these [cases] that we say here, they did not intend to perform the labor; therefore, he is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:3:3.english: With regard to exile - For example, if it fell upon a person and he died.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:3:4.hebrew: פטור - דגבי גלות כתיב "מכה נפש בשגגה" (במדבר ל״ה:י״א), ולא מיקרי שגגה אלא היכא דה"ל ידיעה מעיקרא, וזה לא הכיר בה מעולם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:3:4.english: Exempt - For regarding exile it is written: "[one who] strikes a person unwittingly" (Numbers 35:11), and it is not called "unwittingly" unless he had prior awareness [of it], whereas this [person] never noticed it at all.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:4:1.hebrew: לענין עבד - אם נפלה על עבדו וסימאה עינו, פלוגת' דרשב"ג ורבנן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:4:1.english: With regard to a slave - If [the stone] fell on his slave and blinded his eye, [this is] a dispute between Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and the Rabbis.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:6:1.hebrew: לענין ד' דברים פטור - דאע"ג דהכיר בה, הויא שכחה שוגג ולא פשיעה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:6:1.english: With regard to [the] four types of indemnity [he is] exempt - For even though he was aware of it, forgetting is [considered] unwitting and not negligence.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:6:2.hebrew: לענין שבת פטור - ואע"ג דמקריא שגגה לענין גלות, פטור בשבת, דבעינן מלאכת מחשבת, שנתכוין לעשות מלאכה וכסבור שהיום חול, וזה לא נתכוין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:6:2.english: With regard to Shabbat, he is exempt - Even though it is called unwitting with regard to exile, he is exempt on Shabbat, because we require purposeful labor — that he intended to perform a labor while thinking that today is a weekday — whereas this [person] did not intend [to do so].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:7:1.hebrew: לזרוק שתים וכו' - לענין שבת פטור, דמלאכת מחשבת בעינן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:7:1.english: To throw two [cubits], etc. - With regard to Shabbat, [he is] exempt, for we require planned labor.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:7:2.hebrew: לענין גלות - חייב, דכתיב: "ואשר לא צדה" "ושמתי לך מקום וגו'", פרט למתכוין לזרוק שתים וזרק ארבע — שאינו בתורת "וכי יזיד איש וגו'", אלא בתורת "ושמתי לך מקום וגו'". לישנא אחרינא: "ואשר לא צדה פרט למתכוין כו'" — דפטור מגלות, דהכי משמע: שלא צדה, שלא נתכוין לצדד ולזרוק אצלו, ינוס, פרט לזה שצדה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:7:2.english: With regard to exile - [He is] liable, as it is written: "And if a man lie not in wait," "then I will appoint you a place, etc." — [which] excludes one who intended to throw two [cubits] and threw four, for he is not in the category of "And if a man come presumptuously, etc." [the death penalty], but rather in the category of "then I will appoint you a place, etc." [exile]. Another version: "And if a man lie not in wait — excluding one who intended, etc." — [meaning] that he is exempt from exile, for this is what [the verse] implies: one who "did not lie in wait" — [that is,] he did not intend to aim and throw near him — shall flee, excluding this [person] who did aim [in his direction].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:8:1.hebrew: אם אמר כל מקום שתרצה תנוח - חייב, שהרי יש כאן מלאכת מחשבת דזרק ארבע. אבל נתכוין לזרוק שתים וזרק ארבע, אפילו אמר כל מקום שתרצה תנוח, פטור, שעיקר מחשבתו אינה למלאכה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:8:1.english: If he said, “Wherever it wishes, let it rest” - he is liable, for here there is purposeful labor, since he [intended to] throw four [cubits]. However, [if] he intended to throw two [cubits] and threw four [cubits], even [if] he said, “Wherever it wishes, let it rest,” he is exempt, for his primary intention was not for a [prohibited] labor.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:9:1.english: Threw - The owner of the vessel [threw] a vessel from the top of the roof.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:9:2.hebrew: פטור - זה ששברו במקל קודם שבירתה, שהרי סופה לישבר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 26b:9:2.english: [He is] exempt - This [one] who broke it with a stick before its breaking, for it was destined to break.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:10:1.hebrew: קדם וסילקו - פירש רב אלפס דרבה לטעמיה, דלית ליה דינא דגרמי בריש הגוזל קמא (לקמן בבא קמא דף צח.). ולר"י נראה דהא גרמא בניזקין הוא, ופטור לכולי עלמא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:10:1.english: [Or] he went first and removed it - Rav Alfas explained that Rabbah follows his own reasoning, as he does not hold of [liability for] dina de-garmi [proximate indirect causation] at the beginning of [the chapter] HaGozel Kamma (later in Bava Kamma 98a). But to the Ri it appears that this is gerama [indirect causation] in damages, and he is exempt according to everyone.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:11:1.hebrew: זרק תינוק מראש כו' - לא דמי להרג טריפה, דפטור לכולי עלמא באלו הן הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף עח.):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:11:1.english: [If one] threw a child from the top [of the roof], etc. - It is not similar to [one who] killed a tereifah, who is exempt according to everyone, [as stated] in [the chapter] Eilu Hein HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 78a).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:2:1.hebrew: האי מיבעי ליה ליתן צער במקום נזק - וריפוי ושבת ובושת, כולהו מצער ילפינן דחייב במקום נזק, כדמשמע בהחובל (לקמן בבא קמא דף פה.), דאמר: תנא, וכולן חייבין בתשלומין במקום נזק; מנהני מילי? אמר רב זביד משמיה דרבא: אמר קרא "פצע תחת פצע" כו' — משמע דכולהו ילפינן מצער. ולרב פפא דאמר התם: אמר קרא "ורפא ירפא" ליתן ריפוי במקום נזק — כולהו ילפינן מריפוי. וא"ת, דהכא משמע דצער שלא במקום נזק פשוט טפי, דאיצטריך קרא לצער במקום נזק; ובפרק החובל (שם:) משמע איפכא, דאמר: "צער שלא במקום נזק דמשלם, מאן תנא?" וי"ל, דשלא במקום נזק דלקמן היינו במקום שלא עשה רושם, כדקתני: "כוואו על צפרניו". וצער שלא במקום נזק דהכא היינו על בשרו, שניכר רישומו ולא אפחתיה מכספיה. וצער במקום נזק דהכא כגון קיטע ידו ושיבר רגלו דאפחתיה מכספיה, דההוא לא שמעינן ליה לא מחבורה ולא מכווה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:2:1.english: This [verse] is necessary to impose [payment for] pain in a case of damage - And [as for] medical expenses, loss of livelihood, and humiliation — we derive all of them from [the law of] pain, that one is liable [for them] in a case of damage, as is implied in [the chapter] HaChovel (later, Bava Kamma 85a), where [the Gemara] says: "It was taught: And all of them are liable for payment in a case of damage; from where [in Scripture] are these matters [derived]? Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava: Scripture says, 'wound for wound,' etc." — [this] implies that we derive all of them from pain. And according to Rav Pappa, who says there: "Scripture says, 'and he shall surely heal,' to impose [payment for] medical expenses in a case of damage" — we derive all of them from medical expenses. And if you ask: Here it is implied that pain not in a case of damage is more obvious [to be liable], since a verse is needed for pain in a case of damage; whereas in the chapter HaChovel (ibid., [85]b) the opposite is implied, as [the Gemara] says: "Who is the Tanna [who holds] that one pays for pain not in a case of damage?" And one can answer that "not in a case of damage" later [in HaChovel] refers to a case where he made no mark, as [the Mishnah] teaches: "[If] he burned him on his fingernails." Whereas "pain not in a case of damage" here refers to [an injury] on his flesh, where its mark is visible, yet it did not diminish his monetary value. And "pain in a case of damage" here is, for example, where he severed his hand or broke his leg, which diminished his monetary value — for that [case] we would not derive from either "bruise" or "burn."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:2:2.hebrew: ש"מ תרתי - וא"ת: לעיל אמרינן "סימא עינו של חבירו בשוגג או באונס — נזק אין, ד' דברים לא", צער נמי ליחייב, דבההוא קרא דמרבינן נזק כתיב נמי צער? וי"ל, דכל מה דמצינן למיפטר שוגג פטרינן, ולכך מוקמינן דהאי קרא דמרבה שוגג — דוקא בנזק דאיירי ביה עיקר קרא, ולא בצער:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:2:2.english: Derive two [conclusions] from it - And if you ask: Earlier we said [that if one] blinded his fellow's eye unintentionally or by unavoidable accident, [for] damage — yes [he is liable], [for the other] four items — no [he is not liable]; he should also be liable [for] pain, for in that verse [from which] we include damage, pain is also written? And one can answer: Whatever we are able to exempt [in the case of] an unintentional act, we exempt; and therefore we establish that this verse that includes an unintentional act [applies] specifically to damage, with which the main verse deals, and not to pain.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:4:1.hebrew: לענין עבד פלוגתא דרשב"ג ורבנן - תימה, דבפ"ק דקדושין (דף כד: ושם ד"ה מיבעי) מוקמי רבנן האי "ושחתה" להושיט ידו במעי שפחה וסימא עובר שבמעיה, דפטור משום שלא נתכוין לעין, וה"נ לא נתכוין! וי"ל דלא פטרוהו רבנן אלא היכא דלא נתכוין לעין וגם נתכוין לטובתו של עבד כי התם, אבל הכא לא נתכוין לטובתו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:4:1.english: With regard to a slave, [this is] a dispute between Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and the Rabbis - [This is] surprising, for in the first chapter of Kiddushin (24b, and there, s.v. Mibaei), the Rabbis establish this [phrase] "and he destroys it" [as referring] to [a case where he] reaches his hand into the womb of a maidservant and blinds the fetus in her womb, [teaching] that he is exempt because he did not intend [to strike] the eye — and here too, he did not intend [to strike the eye]! And one can say that the Rabbis only exempted him where he did not intend [to strike] the eye and also intended for the benefit of the slave, like there, but [here, he did not intend for the slave's benefit].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:6:1.hebrew: בשגגה מכלל דה"ל ידיעה - משום דגבי גלות כתיב טובא "בשגגה", דריש לה; דהא גבי חלב, אע"ג דכתיב ביה "בשגגה", לא חיישינן להיתה לו ידיעה. ומהאי טעמא נמי ממעטינן בריש אלו הן הגולין (מכות דף ז: ושם ד"ה אלא) אומר מותר מ"בשגגה" לגבי גלות, אע"ג דגבי שבת וע"ז כתיב "בשגגה" ומחייבינן אומר מותר בפרק כלל גדול (שבת דף סח: ושם):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:6:1.english: "Unwittingly — by inference that he had [prior] awareness" - Because with regard to exile "unwittingly" is written many times, [the Gemara] expounds it [thus]; for behold, with regard to cheilev [forbidden fat], even though "unwittingly" is written concerning it, we are not concerned with his having had [prior] awareness. And for this same reason as well, we exclude at the beginning of [the chapter] Eilu Hen HaGolin (Makkot 7b, and there s.v. Ella) one who says "it is permitted" from "unwittingly" with respect to exile, even though with regard to Shabbat and idolatry "unwittingly" is written, yet we hold liable one who says "it is permitted" in the chapter Kelal Gadol (Shabbat 68b and there).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:7:1.hebrew: נתכוין לזרוק שתים וזרק ארבע כו' - לענין שבת פטור. ואפילו לאביי דמחייב בפרק כלל גדול (שבת דף עג.), היינו נתכוין לזרוק שתים ונמצאו ארבע — דומיא דנתכוין לחתוך התלוש וחתך את המחובר, דהיינו שסבור תלוש ונמצא מחובר; דאי נתכוין לזה וחתך זה, היינו מתעסק, כדמוכח בפרק ספק אכל (כריתות דף יט:):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:7:1.english: He intended to throw two [cubits] and threw four, etc. - With regard to Shabbat, [he is] exempt. And even according to Abaye, who holds [him] liable in the chapter [entitled] Kelal Gadol (Shabbat 73a), that is [a case where] he intended to throw two [cubits] and they turned out to be four — similar to [one who] intended to cut what is detached and cut what is attached, which means that he thought [it was] detached and it turned out [to be] attached; for if he intended [to cut] this [one] and cut that [one], that is mit'asek [acting unawares], as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Safek Akhal (Keritot 19b).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:8:1.hebrew: פרט למתכוין לזרוק כו' - לשון ראשון פי' בקונטרס: פרט למתכוין לזרוק ב' וזרק ארבע, דלא הוי בכלל "כי יזיד". וטפי הוה ניחא לפרש דלא הוי בכלל "מכה איש ומת" דהוי לעיל מינה, מלפרש "כי יזיד" דהוי בתריה. וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך לחייב גלות נתכוין לזרוק שתים וזרק ארבע, דמהיכא ס"ד דפטור? דלפטור ממיתה ודאי לא אתיא, דפשיטא דשוגג פטור ממיתה. וי"ל דמ"בלא צדייה" דריש באלו הן הגולין (מכות דף ז: ושם ד"ה אשר): פרט למתכוין לזרוק בצד זה וזרק בצד אחר, ומהאי קרא הוה פטרינן אפי' נתכוין לזרוק שתים וזרק ארבע. ולפירוש אחרון שפירש בקונטרס שפטור מגלות — קשה קצת, דבפרק אלו הן הגולין אמר: "אם בפתע בלא איבה הדפו" — פרט לשונא; "בלא צדייה" — פרט לנתכוין לזרוק בצד זה והלכה לצד אחר; "ואשר לא צדה" — פרט למתכוין לזרוק שתים וזרק ארבע. והשתא, מ"אשר לא צדה" דכתיב בריש "ואלה המשפטים", הוה ליה למעוטי ההוא דדמי טפי לפטור, כגון נתכוין לזרוק בצד זה, שלא נתכוין לצד הנרצח. וי"ל: משום דהתחיל התנא לדרוש קרא ד"בלא צדייה", נקט ברישא נתכוין לזרוק בצד זה, דרוצה להזכיר הפשוט תחילה. וא"ת: אמאי איצטריך באלו הן הגולין מ"בשגגה" לפטור נתכוין להרוג הבהמה והרג האדם? ע"כ היינו או נתכוין לזרוק בצד זה וזרק בצד אחר, או נתכוין לזרוק שתים וזרק ארבע! וי"ל דהתם איצטריך כגון שהיו הבהמה והאדם זה בצד זה, א"נ כסבור בהמה ונמצא אדם. ותימה: דהא פליגי רבי ורבנן בנשמט הברזל מקתו ומן העץ המתבקע — דמר מחייב בהאי ומר מחייב בהאי בריש אלו הן הגולין — אמאי חייב? והא הוי כמו נתכוין לזרוק שתים וזרק ארבע, שנתכוין לבקע עצים שלפניו והלך למרחוק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:8:1.english: "To exclude one who intended to throw, etc." - In the first explanation, Rashi explained [that it comes] to exclude one who intended to throw two [cubits] and threw four, as he is not included in "if [a man] acts intentionally." And it would have been more satisfactory to explain [that he is excluded from] "He who strikes a man and he dies," which is [written] above it, than to explain [that he is excluded from] "if [a man] acts intentionally," which is [written] after it. And if you ask: Why was it necessary to obligate exile [for] one who intended to throw two [cubits] and threw four — from where would it enter your mind that he is exempt? For to exempt [him] from the death penalty it certainly does not come, since it is obvious that an unintentional [killer] is exempt from the death penalty. And one can say that from "without lying in wait," [the Gemara] expounds in [the chapter] Eilu Hen HaGolin (Makkot 7b, and there s.v. Asher): [This comes] to exclude one who intended to throw in this direction and threw in another direction; and from that verse we would have exempted even one who intended to throw two [cubits] and threw four. And according to the latter explanation that Rashi explained — that he is exempt from exile — it is somewhat difficult, for in the chapter Eilu Hen HaGolin [the Gemara] says: "If suddenly without enmity he pushed him" — excluding an enemy; "without lying in wait" — excluding one who intended to throw in this direction and it went in another direction; "and if he did not lie in wait" — excluding one who intended to throw two [cubits] and threw four. Now, from "and if he did not lie in wait," which is written at the beginning of [the Torah portion] Ve'eileh HaMishpatim, it should have excluded that case which is more similar to being exempt, such as one who intended to throw in this direction, who did not intend [to throw] in the direction of the slain person. And one can say: Because the Tanna began to expound the verse of "without lying in wait," he mentioned first one who intended to throw in this direction, as he wants to mention the more obvious [case] first. And if you ask: Why was it necessary in Eilu Hen HaGolin [to derive] from "unintentionally" to exempt one who intended to kill an animal and killed a person? Perforce, that is either one who intended to throw in this direction and threw in another direction, or one who intended to throw two [cubits] and threw four! And one can say that there it was necessary [for a case] such as where the animal and the person were next to each other, or alternatively, where he thought [it was] an animal and it turned out [to be] a person. And it is astonishing: For Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] and the Rabbis disagree regarding [the case where] the iron [head] slipped from its handle or from the wood being split — where one master obligates [exile] in this case and one master obligates [exile] in that case at the beginning of Eilu Hen HaGolin — why is he liable? After all, it is like one who intended to throw two [cubits] and threw four, since he intended to split the wood in front of him and it went far away!

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:9:1.hebrew: ואמר רבה זרק כלי מראש הגג - רבה גרסינן, דרבא מספקא ליה לעיל (בבא קמא דף יז:) אי בתר מעיקרא אזלינן אי לא, וקאמר דנפשוט מרבה שהוא רבו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 26b:9:1.english: And Rabbah says: [If] one threw a vessel from the roof - We read [the text as] Rabbah, for Rava was uncertain earlier (Bava Kamma 17b) whether we follow the initial [act] or not, and [the Gemara there] says that we should resolve [it] from Rabbah, who is his teacher.
